payload.text:
Record check 2026-09-20 (user has a TypeSafe plan as of today; "parked" no longer applies). Corrections and gaps against the 09-19 audit:

1. Context is 64k total, 32k for state + the longest question (not a flat 32k). Rate limits 250k tokens/s and 1,200 req/min, dynamic; higher on enterprise via sales@typesafe.ai. Current model jev-1.13.0; aliases jev-latest and jev-preview both point at it; GET /v1/models lists what an account may use. Pin the exact version in anything we record, never the alias (same rule as the driver's context_window: state it, never infer).
2. Privacy: "We will not train or fine tune any AI/ML models on your prompts or other Input"; Input is not disclosed except to service providers; retention period unspecified; no zero-data-retention option. So the invariant's privacy clause is softened (no training) but not resolved (content leaves the machine and sits for an unstated time). redact.ts exists and should run before any send.
3. JS SDK is @typesafe-ai/sdk and needs Node ≥20; sofar requires Node ≥18 and CLAUDE.md forbids new deps without a Decision. Use fetch against POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (Bearer TYPESAFE_API_KEY) — zero deps, Node 18 has fetch.
4. Alternative route: Cloudflare Workers AI lists typesafe/jev with no gate (POST /accounts/{id}/ai/run, model typesafe/jev). Not needed now that a direct plan exists.
5. Confidence is a statistic of the distribution: for 3 options (3·pmax−1)/2, i.e. (n·pmax−1)/(n−1); Noul carries none, use |p−0.5|. Docs: no structural invariants across questions (P(A)+P(not A) across two Nouls need not be 1); never carry a threshold from one question type to another; validate thresholds on our own data.
6. jev-1.13 known limitations page: literal reading (scoping words and negations at face value), no counting, weak on numeric representations, dates read as text, indirection and double negatives degrade, large irrelevant state distracts, adversarial state moves the answer, contradictory instructions vs criteria confuse it, no text generation. Consequences for sofar: staleness, counts and timestamps stay in code; state is selected lexically first (the existing index) and only the candidates are sent; agent-written record text is untrusted input, so every judge output is advisory (warning in a tool result), never a mutation, never a block (BD22 best-effort).
7. Self-consistency cookbook: per-question probability std dev 0.0102 across 15 repeats, far below LLMs. Near-deterministic, not byte-deterministic; fold and graph keep their pure contracts and judge outputs live outside them.
8. Structured criteria (what / not_for / examples per option; summary / signals per level) and instructions that cite state paths in backticks are directly usable to encode our decision guards and rejected approaches as criteria.
9. TypeSafe ships a Claude Code plugin (claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai) so the agent itself can call Jev in a session; that is the operator's process and not sofar's concern, but it means a sofar session may already have the skill loaded.
10. Still absent anywhere: architecture paper, public calibration curve, third-party replication. Thresholds must come from our own ground truth (bench-refresh hidden tests, and the record's own history: decisions later superseded, approaches later re-proposed).

The 09-19 waitlist answer note and the roadmap-h2 audit note stand; nothing in them is wrong.

Feature catalogue (2026-09-20): what a cheap calibrated judge unlocks in sofar, grouped by where it can run. Constraint first: 70–500 ms means never on a hook, statusline or shim (speed T2, 100 ms). It fits three places: WRITE time (inside an MCP tool call or the driver between sessions), PULL time (find, related, why, review), and OFFLINE (index pass, tune, bench loss study). Anything a hook must show is judged at write time and stored in the derived index or as an enrichment event with a producer field (the roadmap-h2 design), then read cheaply. Cost is not a factor: ten questions over a full 16k digest is about $0.0007; a heavy day of write-backs is cents.

A. WRITE-TIME GUARDS (highest leverage: the write-back is the event the next session reads first)
A1 Write-back quality gate in sofar_end_session: Score next_action on levels {vague, names a task, names a task and a concrete first step, executable verbatim}; low score returns a warning asking for a better one. Noul "does the summary describe a decision that was not logged?" and "an operational fact worth repo memory?" (the decision / fact / note distinction agents get wrong; repo-memory-capture already wants this).
A2 Re-proposal guard in sofar_log_decision: Noul per rejected approach (criteria built from the rejection text) "does this decision re-propose R?"; warning with the rejected item cited. Directly targets bench claim C3.
A3 Contradiction guard: Noul per standing constraint "does this decision contradict D-n?", same-initiative and cross-initiative (candidates chosen by the existing index, then judged; state stays under 32k). Extends drift-hardening decision guards and cross-initiative-conflicts.
A4 Decision hygiene: Noul "does `because` give a reason or restate the choice?"; Choice {decision, operational fact, note} to route a misfiled write with a hint.
A5 Task-done evidence: on sofar_update_task(done), Noul "does the note cite evidence (test run, commit, criteria)?"; warning only. Acceptance-criteria law made checkable.

B. DRIVER (unattended runs; between sessions, latency irrelevant)
B1 Progress judge: today stall = no status change. Noul over {task text, write-back, diff stat, test output} "did this session advance the task?" plus Score "how done against the acceptance text?"; a task_done handoff needs status AND judged completion. Targets C4 wasted sessions and C5 rework.
B2 Richer handoff reason: Choice {task_done, partial, stalled, blocked_on_user, worked_wrong_task, scope_creep}; needs_user today fires only on status=blocked, but the write-back prose often names an operator decision.
B3 Pre-flight: before launching, Noul "is this task specified well enough to act without asking?"; low → mark needs_user and skip the launch instead of burning a session.
B4 Route hints: Score task complexity on described levels → effort; Choice model; fills only what the run left open (routing.ts rule: run over task).
B5 Next-task sanity: Noul "after this write-back, is the plan's next task still the right one?"; low → nudge the operator, never reorder the plan.

C. INJECTION AND CONTEXT (judged at write time, read by hooks)
C1 Relevance-scored digest: at end_session the next task is known, so Score every decision, note, rejected approach and repo-memory line for relevance to it; store scores in the index; the SessionStart hook injects top-k and truncates the least relevant instead of the last. Small token win (~1% of a session) but a real orientation win (digest-signal goal).
C2 Adjacency to aboutness: "…and 34 more adjacent records" becomes the three that actually bear on the next task (Noul per adjacent initiative).
C3 Constraint classification: at scale, Choice per decision {standing constraint, history, superseded} so "obey verbatim (6)" stays six and not sixty.

D. PULL SURFACES
D1 Semantic re-ranking for find / related / why: candidates from the lexical index, ranked by Score; the citation grammar stays closed and lexical (contract).
D2 Why-questions answered by citation: "why no pid files?" → lexical candidates → Choice over candidate decisions "which answers this?" with confidence → the answer is an id, no text generation needed. Targets C8.

E. OFFLINE
E1 Bench-refresh: a "sofar + judge" arm; Jev as a calibrated blind reviewer for C5; loss-row classification into the D5/D10 taxonomy at near-zero cost.
E2 Tune/suggest: cause labelling is excluded by design; offer at most an opt-in labelled view, never change the detectors.
E3 Calibration study on our own record: judge all ~280 decisions for constraint-vs-history and every rejected approach against later decisions; the record already knows which were superseded or re-proposed, so it is free ground truth for thresholds. This is the right FIRST step: measure before wiring anything.

Architecture for all of it: one Judge seam (noul / choice / score over a state object) with a deterministic default provider (today's counts and lexical rules answering with confidence 1.0 or 0.5) and an opt-in Jev provider via fetch; enrichment events carry producer and model version; redaction before send; outputs advisory only. Needs the opt-in Decision naming SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3 before the provider exists; the seam, the question set and E3 as a scratch script need no ruling.

Suggested order when work opens: E3 (measure) → A1/A2 (write-time guards) → B1/B3 (driver) → C1 (digest) → D2 → E1.

payload.text:
RUST PLACEMENT (2026-09-20). rust-core D1 moves the HOT PATH to Rust: hooks, append, fold, digest/status render, statusline; crates limited to serde, serde_json, ulid. TypeScript keeps the MCP server, drive, init/doctor/review and cloud commands. Every judge use in the catalogue runs at write time (MCP tools), in the driver, on pull surfaces or offline — all TypeScript-kept, and all ruled off the hot path by latency anyway. So the Jev provider is TypeScript via fetch (Node 18, zero deps) and Rust never calls it. Rust only READS judge outputs: enrichment events (schema in packages/schema, Rust types generated) or index files, both already in its contract. If a judge call ever needs to move to Rust it needs an HTTP crate (ureq or reqwest), which is a Decision naming rust-core D1 — not before there is a measured reason.

NETWORK VS JEV for connected memory (user's question): not either/or. The record graph gives truth and the candidate set (cheap, deterministic, 3 ms); Jev's fan-out ranks candidates in ONE parallel request (one Noul per candidate, latency near-flat in question count); code renders the budgeted block from existing projection fields. Full design logged in roadmap-h2 (networked-memory note, 2026-09-20); the deterministic half is a new initiative `linked-context` needing no ruling, the ranked half is C1/C2 here.

- Relevance-scored digest: token effect ~1% of a session (M share); fewer source re-greps on resume (E; digest-signal finding).
- Linked-context travel block: ~2.5k tokens and 1 pull turn saved per cross-record resume (M pull size, E frequency); blocked tasks unblock without a human (new capability).
- Answer packets: C8 why-accuracy up (E); latency 3 ms → ~300 ms (M).
- Jev as bench blind reviewer: ~$0.0007 per judgement, 100x+ cheaper than LLM review, more reps within D9 budget (M price; agreement with human review E).

plan.goal: Adopt the shape of TypeSafe Jev / System One models in sofar: typed judgements (noul, choice, score) over record state with calibrated probabilities and confidence-gated escalation, behind a Judge seam whose default is deterministic and whose Jev provider is explicit opt-in. Judging runs only at write time (MCP tools), in the driver, on pull surfaces or offline — never on a hook, statusline, shim, fold or projection path. phases.name: Phase 1 — Measure on our own record

tasks.title: Calibration script (scratch, outside the engine): build ground truth from the record — decisions with a rule vs without (constraint vs one-off), decision→task mentions (relevance), rejected `over` text vs the chosen line (re-proposal) — and judge them with Jev in fan-out batches under the 32k state cap; report agreement, calibration by confidence bucket, cost and latency
Set provisional thresholds per question type from 1.1 (act / warn / silent) and record them with the model version jev-1.13.0; note which questions are not worth wiring

SPEC: Judge seam contract — question types, state shape, answer shape with probabilities and confidence, provider interface, where judging may run and where it may not, advisory-only rule, redaction before send, model version pinning
Deterministic default provider: today's counts and lexical rules re-expressed as answers with confidence 1.0 or 0.5, tests

Jev provider via fetch (POST /v1/systemone, Bearer TYPESAFE_API_KEY, zero deps, Node 18): retries on 429/529, timeout, redact.ts before send, opt-in via ~/.config/sofar/config.json judge.provider, disabled by default
Enrichment event type in packages/schema for stored judgements (producer, model version, question id, answer, confidence, subject event id); fold ignores them for state, index reads them
A2/A3 in sofar_log_decision: re-proposal and contradiction Nouls over rejected approaches and standing constraints (candidates by index, state under 32k); warning text cites the target
A1 in sofar_end_session: next_action Score on described levels, unlogged-decision and repo-memory-fact Nouls over the summary; warning only
A4/A5: decision-vs-fact-vs-note routing hint; task-done evidence Noul in sofar_update_task
B1 progress judge: handoff reason from a Noul over task text, write-back, diff stat and test output, combined with status; B2 richer reason set
B3 pre-flight: task specified well enough to act; low → needs_user without a launch
B4 route hints: complexity Score → effort, Choice → model, filling only what the run left open
C1/C2: relevance scores for decisions, notes, rejected approaches, repo memory and adjacent initiatives against the next task, judged at write-back, stored in the index, read by the SessionStart hook
D1/D2: judge-ranked find and answer packets (depends on linked-context Phase 5)
E1: sofar + judge arm in bench-refresh; Jev as calibrated blind reviewer; grade the pre-registered predictions

payload.because: Jev defeats only the cost clause of felt-cost D3 (about $0.0007 per full-digest judgement, output free) and TypeSafe contractually does not train on inputs; the privacy and dependency clauses remain, which is why the exception is opt-in, redacted, advisory and confined to paths a hook never touches (70–500 ms against the 100 ms shim budget). A default install still makes zero model calls, so SPEC Architectural invariants holds for everyone who does not opt in; this decision supersedes it and felt-cost D3 for the opted-in judge paths only.
payload.chose: A narrowly scoped exception to the zero-model invariant: sofar MAY call TypeSafe Jev (a typed-decision model, no text generation) as a Judge provider, only when the operator has opted in via config, only from an MCP tool, the driver, a pull command or an explicit offline command, only with redacted state, and only to produce advisory outputs (warnings, rankings, enrichment events stamped with producer and model version). Ruled by the user 2026-09-20 ("let's come back to the Jev implementation") after the audit in roadmap-h2 note 01M2X0KK6MT2AE2A83KWJ3PZX9.
payload.over: Keeping the invariant absolute (leaves every judgement lexical and count-based; the record shows the costs in wasted stall sessions, re-proposals and adjacency-not-aboutness); a general LLM call in the engine (text generation, seconds of latency, unverifiable output — refused in roadmap-h2 note 01M2ZESQFZWVM8TYHXG19YYVZN); a local encoder model shipped with sofar (a new dependency and model weights in the hot path, and the HN finding that the hard part is the answer spaces, not the model).
payload.rule: Never call a model from a hook, statusline, shim, fold or projection path, and never without the operator's opt-in; a judge call runs only inside an MCP tool, the driver, a pull command or an explicit offline command, sends redacted state, and produces advisory output only.

payload.text:
1.1 RESULTS (2026-09-21, jev-1.13.0, scripts/judge-calibration.mjs, raw rows in the session scratchpad calibration.json). 42 requests, 325,265 input tokens, $0.0137, p50 402 ms, max 1,517 ms, 0 lost batches after retries (the first two attempts died on a flaky network: connect timeouts, then DNS; the script now retries 8x and skips a lost batch).

A constraint-vs-one-off (Choice). Whole set 45.9% — meaningless, because 178 of 364 decisions predate the `rule` field and are all labelled one_off; Jev called felt-cost D3, drift-hardening D1, security-hardening D1 constraints at 0.98–1.00 and it is right. Post-rule era only (n=186, 62% constraints): accuracy 71.5%, constraint precision 73.7% / recall 84.5%; by confidence 0–0.5: 63%, 0.5–0.8: 80%, 0.8–0.95: 61%, 0.95–1: 84% (not monotone). Hand-read of the five most confident post-era disagreements: session-driver D7 and D10 are real constraints the agent never marked with a rule (Jev right, label wrong); record-index D8/D13 and self-improve D11 are durable MECHANISMS that Jev reads as rules (Jev wrong). So the residual error is one-directional and a criteria problem: add not_for "a description of how the built software behaves, however durable" to standing_constraint and re-run before wiring 5.1's constraint classification. Even now, "Jev says constraint at ≥0.95 while no rule is set" is a useful WARNING at log_decision time: half of those are missing rules.

B decision-bears-on-task (Noul). n=230, accuracy 67.8%, Brier 0.211; true recall 90.4%, false precision 82.5%; monotone from 0.6 up: 0.6–0.8: 78%, 0.8–1.0: 86%; at p≥0.9 (n=43) precision 86%, at p≤0.1 (n=7) 86%. The confident cross-initiative "false positives" are largely real aboutness the graph cannot see: commit-attribution D4 → hookspath-attribution 1.3 (both attribution via hooks), felt-cost D5 → rust-core 2.5 (hook latency → hook handlers), task-drop-state D1 → stale-session-signals 3.1. One real miss: notes-in-digest D1 → its own 1.1 at 0.07, where the decision IS the task's pre-registration — literal reading of "need to know".

1.2 PROVISIONAL THRESHOLDS (jev-1.13.0, validate again on the next model version):
- Relevance Noul (C1/C2/D1/5.1): carry at p ≥ 0.8 (≈86% right), drop at p ≤ 0.2, 0.2–0.8 = deterministic order decides. Never use relevance to REMOVE a lexically linked item; only to add and to rank.
- Constraint Choice (5.1, and a log_decision hint): warn "reads as a standing constraint — add a rule?" only at confidence ≥ 0.95 and no rule set; silent below. Re-measure after the criteria fix; target ≥85% precision before it renders in a digest.
- General: no action below confidence 0.6 on any question; Noul near 0.5 means undecided, not medium.
Not worth wiring yet: anything that needs A's current criteria in a digest. Worth wiring first: B-shaped relevance (3.1 candidates, 5.1 ranking) and the constraint hint as a warning.
